Definition: to puncture, literally (to perforate, with more or less violence) or figuratively (to specify, designate, libel)
BiblicalUsage: Naqab means to pierce or to bore, and in its sharpest use it means to blaspheme, to pierce the Name with a curse. In Leviticus 24:11 the Israelitish woman's son blasphemes the name of the Lord and curses, and is brought to Moses, and in Leviticus 24:16 whoever blasphemes the name of the Lord shall surely be put to death. In Numbers 23:8 Balaam asks how he shall curse whom God has not cursed, and in 2 Kings 18:21 the staff of Egypt is a bruised reed that will pierce the hand of any man who leans on it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word pierces in both directions, because a curse pierces the Name and a false trust pierces the hand. The blasphemer is stoned because words against God are not small, and the reed is a warning that leaning on Egypt cuts. I hold that my mouth should bless the Name it once could have cursed.
